title: ioctl_do_kdf: out_zero runs on every exit path, not just pre-lock
description:
In src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c ioctl_do_kdf(), the out_free_okm block (line 1892) calls mutex_unlock at line 1897 and then FALLS THROUGH to out_zero at line 1901, which immediately calls mutex_lock again.

The comment at line 1898 states: 'out_zero: reached only from pre-lock validation exits'. This is false. Every path through the locked section (both success and error) reaches out_zero after mutex_unlock, acquiring the mutex a second time.

Consequences:
1. Every ioctl_do_kdf call (success or error from the locked section) does an extra spurious mutex_lock/inbuf_clear/mutex_unlock cycle. inbuf_clear is called twice on error paths (out_inbuf_clear + out_zero), redundantly.
2. The comment is actively misleading — the invariant 'lock is not held at out_zero' is only true for the goto-out_zero paths; for fall-through paths the lock was already released.
3. This is NOT a deadlock since kernel mutexes are non-recursive and the lock was released before re-acquisition. But it is wrong behavior and the comment documents a false invariant.

Fix: add 'return ret;' between the mutex_unlock at line 1897 and the out_zero: label, so out_zero is truly only reached from pre-lock exits. Remove the lock/unlock from out_zero entirely for pre-lock paths by instead calling inbuf_clear under a fresh trylock, or document that inbuf may not yet exist. Alternatively, restructure to use a single cleanup path.
